notes:
- Le Chonk rounds: every 4-7 rounds a special round replaces the zombies with a swarm of Le Chonk:
  chubby spotted seal plushes (modelled on the classic plush, smug face and all) that bounce in fast
  through the windows and bite. They bark, chomp and burst into stuffing; the last one drops a Max Ammo.
  Le Chonk rounds have their own jingle.
- Round-start jingle: every round now starts with an ominous drone, timpani and bell motif.
- Maps are about 2x bigger: 16 rooms instead of 10, and rooms usually come out a size larger than
  their template (longer corridors, bigger cell blocks, halls and yards). Gate prices still rise with
  distance, the upgrade machine is still at least 4 rooms out, and every map keeps all perks and the box.
- Zombies remodelled at twice the detail: rot patches, veins and open wounds on the skin; torn
  clothes with skin showing through, frayed edges, grime and blood drips; exposed ribs or skull on some;
  hair tufts; bone sticking out of arm stumps.
- Zombie animation: heads loll on loose necks, zombies reach for you with grasping hands when close,
  rock back and slow down when shot (bigger hits rock harder), and twitch now and then.
- Hand Cannon reload: a detailed cylinder with six real chambers and flutes. You can see the loaded
  rounds (brass rims and primers at the back, bullets at the front); the ejector throws the empty brass
  out, the chambers are empty, and a speedloader brings in six fresh rounds.
- Thumper fires a real grenade: it flies in an arc with a smoke trail and explodes on impact.
- Fixed a crash on some Outskirts layouts where the start street had no wall for the starting SMG.
